title: Contracts & Commercial Administrator
description:
Contracts & Commercial Administrator

Location: Maidstone, Kent

Hours: Full-time, Monday to Friday

Contract: Permanent

ABOUT THE ROLE

Are you highly organised, commercially aware, and confident managing contracts from start to finish? We are recruiting on behalf of a successful client based in Maidstone for a proactive and detail-driven Contracts Coordinator to join their team.

This is a varied and fast-paced role that will suit someone who enjoys coordinating multiple priorities, maintaining accurate documentation, and building strong relationships with customers, suppliers, and internal teams.

- Liaise with customers, suppliers, contractors, and internal teams to ensure contractual requirements are met
- Prepare, review, and maintain contracts, variations, purchase orders, and supporting documentation
- Monitor contract deadlines, renewals, key dates, and deliverables

- Confident managing multiple priorities and working to deadlines

title: Document Controller
description:
Document Controller
Location: Maidstone, Kent
Salary: £26,000-£30,000 per annum, depending on experience, plus package
Job Type: Permanent
Sector: Mechanical & Electrical
The Opportunity
Damicor is recruiting for a Document Controller to join an established construction business based in Maidstone.
This is an excellent opportunity for an organised and detail-oriented individual to play a key role in supporting project teams by ensuring all project documentation is accurately managed, maintained and distributed.
Previous experience within the Mechanical & Electrical (M&E) or wider construction sector would be highly advantageous, although candidates with strong document control experience in other industries will also be considered.
Key Responsibilities
- Manage and maintain project documentation, ensuring records are accurate and up to date.
- Control the issuing, receipt, revision and distribution of drawings, specifications and technical documents.
- Maintain document registers and ensure information is stored correctly within company systems.
- Liaise with project managers, engineers, subcontractors and other stakeholders.
- Monitor document revisions to ensure teams are working from the latest information.
- Support the preparation of project reports, handover documentation and O&M manuals.
- Ensure documentation complies with company procedures and project requirements.

About You
- Previous experience in a Document Controller or similar administrative role.
- Experience within M&E, building services or construction would be advantageous.
- Strong organisational skills and excellent attention to detail.
- Confident using Microsoft Office and document management systems.
- Excellent communication skills and the ability to work effectively within a busy project environment.
- A proactive approach with the ability to manage competing priorities.

What's on Offer?
- Salary of £26,000-£30,000, depending on experience.
- Additional benefits and package.
- The opportunity to join an established construction business.
- A supportive working environment with opportunities for professional development.

Apply Now
If you're an organised Document Controller looking for your next opportunity in the construction or M&E sector, we'd like to hear from you.

title: Logistics Coordinator - Operations & Quality
company: Pearson Whiffin Recruitment Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Logistics Coordinator - Quality and Operations

£30,000 - £31,000

Monday to Friday, office-based position

Mid Kent

We are currently supporting a well-established manufacturing business in the Maidstone area with the recruitment of a Logistics & Quality Coordinator.

This is a varied role suited to someone who enjoys a combination of coordination, administration and hands-on operational work. You'll work closely with teams across the business, including production, warehouse and logistics, helping to ensure orders are prepared and dispatched accurately and on time.

The role would suit someone with experience in dispatch, logistics, warehouse administration or manufacturing, who is comfortable working across both office and operational environments.

Duties:
- Coordinating deliveries and collections with transport providers
- Preparing shipping and delivery documentation and keeping records up to date
- Using an ERP system to process orders, stock movements and dispatch information
- Carrying out basic quality and quantity checks before goods are dispatched
- Monitoring stock levels and supporting inventory checks
- Liaising with customers and internal teams regarding deliveries and order requirements
- Supporting the warehouse and production teams with picking, packing and preparing goods for dispatch
- Investigating and escalating any delivery, quality or operational issues
- Producing basic reports and maintaining accurate administration
- Working in line with company health and safety procedures

What We're Looking For:

We're looking for someone who is naturally organised, practical and enjoys working in a busy environment. You don't need to have experience in every part of the role, but you'll ideally bring some experience from a logistics, dispatch, manufacturing or warehouse setting.

You'll be confident using computer systems, comfortable dealing with different people throughout the day and have a good eye for detail. Experience with SAP or another stock/ERP system would be useful.

The role also has a hands-on element, so you'll need to be happy getting involved on the operational side rather than being purely office-based. Experience with deliveries, transport companies, stock or quality checks would be a bonus.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone reliable, proactive and willing to get stuck in.

title: Clinical Administrator
description: This is a key role within our multidisciplinary team, supporting clinicians by ensuring incoming clinical correspondence is reviewed, processed and accurately recorded. You will identify relevant clinical information, update patient records and ensure correspondence is directed to the right person or team. The role will suit someone who enjoys working with detailed information, follows processes carefully and can use their judgement to identify what can be safely managed and what needs clinical input. You will help reduce unnecessary GP workload while recognising when something is outside your remit and needs to be escalated. Day-to-day work may include reviewing hospital letters, investigation results and other clinical correspondence, extracting and coding relevant information, updating patient records, filing documentation and directing tasks to the appropriate team. You may also support note summarising and other activities that maintain clear, accurate clinical records. Accuracy and patient safety are at the heart of this role. You will need to manage your workload, follow practice and national guidance, and know when to seek advice from a GP, supervisor or manager. By ensuring clinical information is handled accurately, promptly and safely, you will help our clinicians work effectively and support patient care. As a Clinical Administrator, you will help keep the practices clinical and administrative processes running smoothly. Your main duties will include processing incoming clinical correspondence, accurately updating patient records, reviewing and coding clinical information, and ensuring information is directed to the appropriate team member. You will support the processing of hospital and clinic letters, results, safeguarding information and electronic data, as well as summarising new patient records, supporting registrations and managing out-of-area correspondence. Working closely with the clinical team, you will identify and escalate complex or sensitive issues appropriately and support effective communication across the practice. You will also contribute to team meetings and training and help new colleagues learn practice processes. High standards of confidentiality, information governance and accuracy are essential. Job Description Clinical Administrator Job Title: Clinical Administrator Responsible to: Administration Lead, Practice Manager Accountable to: Practice Partnership Hours: Applicants must be available to work within our core operating hours of 08:00-17:30 . We are open to discussing flexibility around shift length and working patterns for the right candidate. Job Summary The Clinical Administrator provides vital support to the multidisciplinary team by managing and processing clinical correspondence and patient records in line with practice and national guidelines. The role focuses on streamlining workflows to reduce unnecessary GP administration, ensuring accurate coding and filing of information, and directing more complex items to the appropriate clinician for review. The post-holder will work as part of the Clinical Administration team, prioritising their workload effectively, maintaining strict confidentiality at all times, and knowing when to escalate matters to supervisors or clinicians. Roles and Responsibilities Ensure all incoming and internal correspondence is stored in patient records. Review and Read Code clinical correspondence before forwarding to clinicians. Process and file hospital letters, reports, emails and other correspondence. Code diagnoses, procedures and investigations accurately. Refer complex or high-risk documents, including safeguarding issues, to the relevant clinician. Summarise new patient records (manual and GP2GP) and process registrations, transfers, and out-of-area notifications. Manage incoming test results, redirect unmatched pathology, and process screening and monitoring results. Process Out of Hours reports and other external communications. Monitor the practice email inbox, flagging urgent queries promptly. Provide administrative cover for other team members when necessary. Open, scan, distribute and file post; manage photocopying and record requests. Assist with training and mentoring of new staff. Maintain a tidy office environment and adhere to a clear desk policy. Teamwork & Communication Work as part of the Clinical Administration Team and the wider practice team. Build effective working relationships with colleagues, patients and external organisations. Communicate clearly and professionally, ensuring confidentiality at all times. Participate in meetings and training, including occasional sessions outside normal hours. General Responsibilities Confidentiality Patients entrust the practice with sensitive information and staff must respect this confidentiality at all times. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues or the practice may only be shared in line with GDPR and practice policies. Health & Safety Follow practice health and safety policies, including infection prevention and control. Use personal security systems as required. Identify risks, manage work safely, and report concerns promptly. Maintain work areas in a safe, hazard-free condition. Equality & Diversity Promote equality of opportunity and respect the rights of patients, carers and colleagues. Act in ways that recognise diversity and ensure fairness, consistent with policy and legislation. Respect privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs at all times. Personal & Professional Development Participate in annual appraisal and performance reviews. Take responsibility for ongoing learning and development. Share skills and knowledge with colleagues and support new staff training. Quality Strive to maintain quality and safety within the practice. Reflect on individual and team activities, suggesting improvements to enhance performance. Manage own time, workload and resources effectively. Communication Communicate effectively with patients, carers, colleagues and external agencies. Adapt communication methods to meet individual needs and ensure understanding. Other Information Duties may change according to practice needs, following consultation and training. The role is subject to the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act (1974) exceptions, requiring disclosure of relevant convictions. The practice operates a non-smoking policy.
